clusters.name: Stepfather strain and father's remarriage, 1987
clusters.reason: Around the time Jonah began secondary school, his relationship with his stepfather Desmond remained distant while his bond with his father stayed warm. His stepfather and father separated briefly over starting a family, and Jonah's anxiety rose as he made the city chess squad and felt out of his depth.

clusters.name: Grandfather's death and family upheaval, 1989–1992
clusters.reason: Within three years starting in 1989, Jonah's grandfather Gordon died after kidney disease, his mother's partner Desmond moved into a rebuilt house with him, his anxiety rose around late nights, he fused closely with his roommate Rafe at conservatory, suffered a wrist injury that ended his playing, and his functioning fell sharply. His mother filled in his college forms and he let it happen; he was lost and low with no footing as his grandfather died and his mother prepared to remarry.
clusters.change: You moved through a cluster of losses and changes: your grandfather Gordon died in 1991, you were injured and stopped playing, Rafe moved out, and you drifted without direction through 1992 while your mother was settling into her life with Desmond.

clusters.name: Performance peak and relationship split, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: Jonah bonded with Joelle around 1998 and played at his best, winning competitions. Within a year his insomnia worsened before concerts, they separated, and he started therapy. His functioning rose even as his symptom of sleeplessness grew, and the relationship shift toward his therapist Victor came after the split.

clusters.name: Burnout, depression, and grandmother's death, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Starting in 2001, Jonah's anxiety rose and functioning fell as he ran out of steam for performing. His grandmother Winifred was found to have bowel cancer around the same time. He had a disastrous audition in 2002, withdrew from family and friends, left Thornbury, and bonded with Marisol. They split within months and he sank into deep depression through late 2003. He could not face his parents but relied on friends, began swimming, returned to his therapist, and his functioning began to improve. His grandmother died in February 2004, and his anxiety remained high as he struggled to connect with family across these years.
clusters.change: Around 2001 you hit a wall with performing, your grandmother got cancer, and things fell apart over the next few years: the failed audition, a broken relationship, depression, and your inability to reach your parents while everything was happening.

clusters.name: Nursing school and mother cutoff, 2008
clusters.reason: In 2008, Jonah's grandmother Lorna and grandfather Clifford both died. As he prepared for nursing school, he took a building break with Silas at Alder Creek where he was too drained for contact with his mother. She pressed him to visit despite his refusal, they had conflict at the visit, and he cut off contact with her when he left for Marlow Sound in August. His anxiety rose around her pressure to visit. His aunt Imogen had a stroke around this time.
clusters.change: With both your grandparents dying in early 2008 and nursing school ahead, you and your mother hit a breaking point at Alder Creek. You stopped speaking when you moved to Marlow Sound that August, and the silence held for about a year.

clusters.name: Marriage, partner's family fusion, and sleep crisis, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Jonah married Wren in March 2017 and contact with his mother eased slightly. His cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2017. His sister Tara married and his aunt Imogen's memory loss worsened and she began lashing out. Through 2019, Jonah's anxiety rose constantly as he felt driven to push projects forward. In October 2019, Wren became swamped with family events while her family fused tightly around her father and brother. Jonah overfunctioned trying to settle her, his anxiety spiked around family occasions, and at the lake weekend for Wren's mother's retirement he had no sleep from the small hours and could only withdraw as the family rose. His anxiety stayed high afterward on the quiet drive home. His job had steadied and paid well earlier that year, yet his baseline anxiety remained high.
clusters.change: After you married Wren in 2017, the balance shifted: you saw your mother a bit less, you were drawn into Wren's tightly connected family, and by late 2019 you were running on empty at family occasions—unable to sleep, overfunctioning to manage her stress, and feeling you didn't belong.
